title: Fraud Detection for E-Commerce Payments
description:
Online shops and payment providers must decide within the payment flow whether a card-not-present transaction is legitimate. Fraud often shows up as patterns rather than single signals: a burst of purchases within minutes, a new device, a country the customer never shopped from, amounts far above the customer's usual spending. The goal is a system that scores every transaction in real time with machine learning on behavioral and velocity features, and either approves it, asks for additional verification or declines it.

Requirements

  • A decision before authorization, within the latency budget of the checkout.
  • Features computed from the customer's recent history without using information from the future.
  • Three outcomes: approve, step-up verification (for example 3-D Secure), decline.
  • A reason for every decision that analysts and support staff can understand.
  • Scales to peak shopping days and fits into existing event streams.

Challenges

  • Fraud is rare (well below 1 % of transactions), so the classes are highly imbalanced.
  • Every false positive blocks or annoys a real customer.
  • Labels (chargebacks) arrive weeks later, and fraud patterns change over time.
goals:
• Scoring latency below 50 ms per transaction at the 99th percentile, including feature lookup.
  • False-positive rate below 0.5 % at the review threshold, measured on a later time period than the training data.
  • Recall on confirmed fraud reported and tracked monthly on the same time-based split.
  • Every decision stored with its score and its top reasons.
